title: JWST/NIRSpec Micro-Shutter Throughput Loss Sandbox
question: Conditional on a planned MSA shutter opening, how do target-centering error and wavelength-dependent PSF width alter simplified geometric slit throughput, and what is the separate penalty under a conservative 4% command-failure scenario?
gap: An instrument-physics QA sandbox; not a replacement for the JWST pipeline or official path-loss corrections.
dataMode: official instrument parameters + synthetic Monte Carlo
criticalCorrection: The 0.7795 headline is retired. It incorrectly multiplied conditional slit transmission by an aggregate planning-operability fraction. The corrected primary estimate is 0.9490 conditional geometric throughput; a separate conservative 4% random non-opening scenario gives 0.9100 effective throughput. Neither is a forecast for a specific observation.
novelty: An instrument-physics QA sandbox built from verified public NIRSpec instrument parameters; not a replacement for the JWST pipeline or official path-loss corrections, and not a novel scientific claim beyond this bounded model.
validationContract: throughput bounds (clipped to [0,1], checked every trial)
0–4% commanded-open failure sensitivity separated from planning operability
injection-recovery of a known effective centering sigma
methodology: Each trial draws a 2D target-centering offset (Gaussian, fiducial sigma=20 mas) and a wavelength uniform on 0.6-5.3 micron. Conditional geometric throughput is computed through the rectangular aperture with a Gaussian-equivalent PSF calibrated to 80 mas FWHM at 2.5 micron. A separate 96% commanded-open success scenario represents the current STScI statement that up to 4% of shutters otherwise classified as operable may remain closed. Static failed, vignetted, short-masked, and failed-open shutters are excluded from throughput: APT/MPT handles them with a position-specific planning map.
assumptions: PSF modelled as a circularly-symmetric 2D Gaussian, not the true NIRSpec Airy/diffraction pattern with wings.
Pure diffraction-limited lambda/D PSF scaling applied across the full 0.6-5.3 micron NIRSpec range, though the literature anchor only confirms Strehl>0.8 above 2.46 micron (VERIFICATION_PENDING).
The 4% non-opening boundary is simulated independently only as a conservative scenario; real command failures and static operability are spatially structured.
Field-averaged shutter pitch/open-area values used; true values vary ~1-4% across the field of view due to optical distortion.
limitations: An instrument-physics QA sandbox; not a replacement for the JWST pipeline or official path-loss corrections.
Models only geometric slit-loss throughput; does not include detector QE, optical-train reflectivity or grating efficiency.
All output is synthetic Monte Carlo data built from verified real instrument parameters, never real NIRSpec telemetry.
The random non-opening term is a sensitivity boundary from current STScI documentation, not a calibrated probability for a particular target, configuration, or epoch.
